parsed_response.reasoning: In GoogleCalendarService, the diff replaces `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` with `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and then persists `data: { key }`. parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result object (`refreshTokenResponse`, i.e. `{success, data}`), not the parsed data, so credential.key is overwritten with the wrapper object; subsequent reads of `googleCredentials.access_token` / `.refresh_token` break for all Google users in the default (non-sharing) path. Same wrapper-vs-data mismatch is visible at other call sites (e.g. Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` only conditionally and drops the previous failure handling).

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full zod safeParse result ({success, data}), and this call site stores that wrapper object directly as credential.key instead of the parsed credential. In the default (non-sharing) configuration, the first Google token refresh overwrites credential.key with {success:true, data:{...}}; every subsequent read of credential.key.access_token / .refresh_token returns undefined, so all Google Calendar operations fail and every Google-connected user must re-authenticate — persistent credential corruption for all deployments.
